messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: An eye exam before starting treatment may be recommended for some people to assess their risk.
Tell your doctor if you have a history of seizures before starting this medicine.
Tell your doctor if you have conditions that potentially increase your risk of seizures.
Manic episodes may be triggered by Fluoxetine.
These episodes include racing thoughts.
They also include reckless behavior.
They include a drastically reduced need for sleep.
They include unusual bursts of energy or irritability.
Changes in appetite or weight can occur.
Weight and appetite changes can occur.
Some patients have significant weight loss.
Children and adolescents should have their height and weight monitored regularly during treatment.
Low sodium (hyponatremia): Low blood sodium levels can occur, particularly in older adults.
Symptoms include headache, weakness, confusion, and difficulty concentrating.
Heart rhythm changes include QT prolongation.
Fluoxetine can affect the heart's electrical activity.
This effect can potentially cause a serious and life-threatening irregular heartbeat.
Triples: [["Fluoxetine", "has administration instruction", "eye exam before starting treatment"], ["Fluoxetine", "has administration instruction", "tell doctor about history of seizures before starting"], ["Fluoxetine", "has administration instruction", "tell doctor about conditions that increase risk of seizures"], ["Fluoxetine", "can trigger", "manic episodes"], ["manic episodes", "include symptom", "racing thoughts"], ["manic episodes", "include symptom", "reckless behavior"], ["manic episodes", "include symptom", "drastically reduced need for sleep"], ["manic episodes", "include symptom", "unusual bursts of energy or irritability"], ["Fluoxetine", "has side effect", "changes in appetite or weight"], ["Fluoxetine", "has side effect", "weight and appetite changes"], ["Fluoxetine", "has side effect", "significant weight loss in some patients"], ["Fluoxetine", "has administration instruction", "monitor height and weight in children and adolescents"], ["Fluoxetine", "has side effect", "low sodium levels"], ["low sodium levels", "more common in", "older adults"], ["low sodium levels", "has symptom", "headache"], ["low sodium levels", "has symptom", "weakness"], ["low sodium levels", "has symptom", "confusion"], ["low sodium levels", "has symptom", "difficulty concentrating"], ["Fluoxetine", "can cause", "heart rhythm changes"], ["Fluoxetine", "has mechanism of action", "affect heart's electrical activity"], ["heart rhythm changes", "include", "QT prolongation"], ["QT prolongation", "can cause", "serious and life-threatening irregular heartbeat"]]
Relations: ["can cause", "can trigger", "has administration instruction", "has mechanism of action", "has side effect", "has symptom", "include", "include symptom", "more common in"]
Answer:

completion:
can cause: The subject entity may lead to or result in the medical condition or effect specified by the object entity.  
can trigger: The subject entity may provoke or initiate the medical condition or event specified by the object entity.  
has administration instruction: The subject drug requires the specific action or precaution specified by the object entity to be followed during its administration.  
has mechanism of action: The subject entity functions or operates through the physiological or pharmacological process specified by the object entity.  
has side effect: The subject drug may produce the adverse or unintended effect specified by the object entity.  
has symptom: The medical condition specified by the subject entity is characterized by the symptom or manifestation specified by the object entity.  
include: The subject entity encompasses or contains the component or aspect specified by the object entity.  
include symptom: The medical condition specified by the subject entity is associated with the symptom or manifestation specified by the object entity.  
more common in: The medical condition or effect specified by the subject entity is more frequently observed in the group or population specified by the object entity.
